discovery: Electron spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realisation of coherent single- and two-qubit control

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

nominees.name: Seigo Tarucha
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (semiconductor spin qubits)
motivation: Loss's 1998 proposal (with DiVincenzo) showed that the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a qubit, controlled by gate voltages and exchange coupling. Turning this into reality required pushing nanofabrication and measurement to their limits. Vandersypen's group achieved single-shot readout of one electron spin and coherent spin rotations, and later built high-fidelity multi-qubit processors in silicon. Tarucha pioneered few-electron quantum dots and micromagnet-driven spin control, which enabled fidelities above 99% and fault-tolerance thresholds in silicon. Together these advances established a new quantum platform in the same material that underpins modern electronics. It is now being scaled with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits; this is the complementary, microscopic route, in which individual electron spins are controlled one at a time.
